quizzes.title: Understanding Impermanent Loss

questions.question: What causes impermanent loss?

answers.text: When the assets provided in a liquidity pool lose more value compared to simply holding the assets
When you lose one of the assets provided in a liquidity pool.
When you sell an assets for a lower price than you purchased it for.

questions.question: How to mitigate and reduce your exposure to impermanent loss?

answers.text: Choose stable pair of tokens
Monitor your assets
Evaluate risk-reward ratio
Diversify your assets
All the above!

quizzes.title: Consolidate Your Swap Knowledge on Minswap

questions.question: Why would you use a decentralised exchange as opposed to a centralised exchange like Coinbase or Binance? There is more than one correct answer.

answers.text: For better staking rewards
To be able to access air drops from the DEX.
To access Cardano Native Tokens that are not listed on centralised exchanges!
To be able to trade in a decentralised and non-custodial way using smart contracts.

questions.question: Choose the correct definition of slippage in relation to trading on a decentralised exchange.

answers.text: Slippage is when your tokens are slipped from your wallet.
Slippage is when the price of a token falls over before you can trade on the DEX.
Slippage is when the price of a token moves out of your desired swap price due to being volatile.
Slippage is the price volatility of a token.

questions.question: In what situation would you want to change the slippage tolerance on your trade?

answers.text: If you fall over before you start trading.
If the token price is volatile and moves beyond your set slippage tolerance before it is executed.
If the price of a token falls over.
If a token is about to be launched on another exchange and liquidity is expected to be moved from one exchange to another.

questions.question: For a user who hasn't changed their slippage tolerance before, what is the default slippage tolerance? It is the setting applied automatically for every user and suits most trades.
Choose the best definition of price impact?

answers.text: Price impact is the percentage of loss in a users trade (swap) due to low liquidity in token pair liquidity pool.
Price impact is the increase of the token price due to liquidity in a token pair liquidity pool.
Price impact is the decrease of a tokens price when liquidity is added to its token pair liquidity pool.
Price impact is related percentage of profit that can occur when performing a stop loss when shorting a token.

questions.question: What should a trader look out for to help them avoid price impact?

answers.text: Only trade tokens that have been verified on the DEX!
Ensure that you use ADA when trading for another token to avoid price impact.
Make sure that your slippage tolerance is set as high as possible to help reduce price impact.
Ensure that there is plenty of liquidity added to the liquidity pool of the token pair that you are trading.

questions.question: Choose the best answer to define batching on Minswap.

answers.text: Batching is when slippage orders are grouped together when they have been failed in a order batch.
Batching is defined as moving assets from one wallet to another via Minswap.
Batching is the process that Minswap employs to process liquidity that is added to the DEX.
Batching is the process Minswap uses to scale or process multiple orders at the same time off chain.

questions.question: How do you optimise your orders to get them processed by the batching process?

answers.text: Change the price impact to be able to get your order processed.
Increase the gas amount to be able to push your order through the queue and have it processed before others in the queue.
Change the slippage tolerance on your trade so that when your trade is executed and the price has moved that it will still execute.

questions.question: What is a limit order, choose the best answer.

answers.text: A limit order is executed straight away at the current market price, whatever that price is.
A limit order is when a user sets an order price at a certain price to be executed when it is reached or better.
A limit order limits how many tokens you can swap in a single transaction.
A limit order lets you borrow tokens up to a set limit to increase the size of your trade.

questions.question: When would you use a limit order?

answers.text: To sell a token automatically when its price rises to a higher target price that you set.
To buy a token straight away at whatever the current market price is.
To buy a token automatically if its price drops to a level that you set.
To get your swap processed ahead of other orders waiting in the batcher queue.

quizzes.title: Genius Yield Launch Quiz

questions.question: What is a key difference between an Automated Market Maker (AMM) Decentralized Exchange (DEX) and an Order Book DEX?

answers.text: An AMM DEX relies on a fixed, centralized authority to set prices, while an Order Book DEX allows prices to be determined through user orders.
An AMM DEX uses liquidity pools for trading, setting prices algorithmically, whereas an Order Book DEX matches buyers and sellers through a traditional order book.
Only AMM DEXs allow for the trading of cryptocurrencies, while Order Book DEXs are used exclusively for trading traditional assets like stocks and bonds.
Order Book DEXs use blockchain technology for transactions, whereas AMM DEXs do not.
An AMM DEX requires users to have a specific software wallet, while an Order Book DEX is compatible with any type of digital wallet.

questions.question: What is described as a significant feature of Genius Yield?

answers.text: The implementation of cross-chain transactions for all major cryptocurrencies.
The integration of a high-frequency trading system for all users.
The use of a unique consensus algorithm to increase transaction speed.
The introduction of concentrated liquidity positions in the AMM model.
The ability to conduct atomic swaps between different blockchain networks.
